editorial:
Imagine working for the biggest company in the world and finding out they are lying to everyone. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow Frances, a smart engineer who realizes her bosses care more about money than people's safety. She teams up with Jeff, a tough reporter from the Wall Street Journal, to leak a mountain of secret files. The vibe is like a high-stakes race against time. You will feel the tension as they try to stay one step ahead of the company's lawyers and security teams while trying to tell the truth to the public.

What really makes this work is the fast talking and the great acting. The dialogue feels real and snappy, which keeps you from getting bored during the slower parts. While some of the legal talk can get a bit heavy, the emotional payoff is huge. If you love stories about underdogs taking on giant corporations, you need to see this. For the best experience, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the detail, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Frances testifies in front of the government. The big twist comes when she reveals a hidden set of documents that proves the company knew about the harm they were causing years ago. This evidence is the final nail in the coffin. The movie wraps up with the company facing massive fines and Frances finding peace, knowing she did the right thing even though her life changed forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories and corporate thrillers.
